newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Cofinec announces new restructuring steps.
newsitem.headline: Cofinec announces new restructuring steps.

text.p: French-registered and Budapest-listed packaging firm Cofinec announced new steps in the group-wide restructuring program it began in September 1996.

The measures include the completion of the merger of its two Hungarian units, the acquisition of minority interests in them, the development of a new holding company structure and the creation of a group incentive and compensation program.

Cofinec Hungary Rt, set up by the merger of Petofi Nyomda es Csomagoloanyagipari Rt and Kner Nyomda Rt as of July 1, expects an annual turnover of around 20 billion forints ($99.9 million) and a production volume of 40,000 tonnes, it said in a statement.
"Prior to the completion of the merger, Cofinec offered to acquire the minority interests held by management, employees and local municipalities, in the Hungarian subsidiaries," it said.

The acquisition, which will be completed through a $4.5 million convertible financing and which is expected to enhance earnings, will result in the 99.9 percent consolidation of the company's ownership of Cofinec Hungary.
The obligation can be converted into Cofinec shares, subject to prior shareholder approval, it added.
The measures announced on Wednesday include a proposal to set up a new parent company for the Cofinec group in the Netherlands, with future investment to be made through it.
"The reorganised holding structure will provide for reduced costs, more flexible corporate governance and an improved tax environment," it said, but did not elaborate on the Netherlands company.

The new incentive programme includes a Cofinec stock option plan, to be fully implemented by the end of the third quarter, which will replace the previous subsidiary-level stock option plan at Petofi and Kner, it said.

The Supervisory Board has authorised the award of 150,000 stock options, representing 4.6 percent of Cofinec's shares capital on a fully diluted basis, to the chairman of the supervisory board and the members of group management.

The chairman of the supervisory board, Pehr Gyllenhammar, former CEO of AB Volvo and board of director member of FMC Corp, Pearson and Reuters and United Technologies, announced he will extend his tenure as chairman beyond the original one-year commitment announced last September.
